svg.title: System lifecycle — the states the whole app shares, and where a user gets stuck
svg.desc: States are combinations of facts, not screens: setup_complete, a rootfs on disk, health, whether the server answers, and who holds the environment lock. Edges are labelled with the guard that allows them, cited to file:line. Red states are dead ends. Read this before drawing any per-area diagram, and reuse these state names verbatim.
svg.text: System lifecycle — where a user gets stuck

DEAD ENDS, WORST FIRST — each with the guard that creates it and what would open it
1 · TRAP — a stale "busy" flag locks every deep operation, permanently
A download service killed before reaching a terminal state leaves EnvironmentLock.isBusyNow() true. Unlike the durable owner marker, it carries no session token,
no timestamp and no expiry, so nothing ever clears it. Clone, backup, restore, module install and the dashboard rebuild all refuse, all with the same wrong message.
env/EnvironmentLock.java:69-87, 97-100 — the file names this itself and points at ADFA-4874.
Opens with: a timestamp on the busy state and an age past which it is ignored, or the durable token treatment the owner marker already has.
2 · TRAP — a hung install holds the boot gate with no timeout at all
Every other gate branch has a safety timer; the installing branch deliberately has none, so the gate lifts only on a terminal install state. If the pipeline never
posts one, Back backgrounds the app and reopening re-enters the same branch. Force-stop is the only way out, and force-stop does not clear the install marker.
Opens with: a long backstop that shows the recovery dialog rather than lifting the gate — the honest answer for a run that stopped reporting.
3 · ONE-WAY — the door a user could choose is shut; the one that opens on failure is not
ADFA-5116 removed both Skip buttons and it worked: verified on the updated tree, every wizard path now installs, clones, or returns to the wizard. Download
deliberately does not mark setup complete (ADFA-4982), and Step 1's Back routes through Library, which bounces straight back. Nothing is left to opt out with.
What remains is not a choice, which is why it is harder to see. "Copy from a phone" marks setup complete before any transfer exists, and a first install marks it
when the install STARTS rather than when it succeeds — so a failed install, a failed clone, or a reinstall that destroys the rootfs without finishing all land in
S1. From there the app routes to Library forever and never offers the wizard again, because none of the four writers ever sets the flag false.
Writers: WizardActivity:308 (Copy) · SetupLibraryActivity:284 (install start) · MainActivity:276 · SetupSectionFragment:245. Read at LibraryActivity:84.
Opens with: writing it on a verified install rather than on intent, and clearing it wherever a rootfs is destroyed — the five destructive routes ADFA-5070 hooks.
4 · HIDDEN EXIT — with no system, the only way forward is named "Get more"
The header says "No library yet — tap Get more to install and add content", which is honest, but it is text with no button, on a row deliberately made
non-clickable, pointing at a control at the far bottom of the screen whose name says content rather than system. Meanwhile every card offers Install and Schedule,
which route to a hub that refuses. A user who does not read is offered two wrong doors and one unlabelled right one.
LibraryHomeFragment.java:555, 575, 585-588 (no action on H_NO_LIBRARY) · 244-252 (Get more) · ModuleHubFragment.java:233-243 (the refusal).
5 · TRAP — a damaged system reached by the wrong door is never diagnosed
The recovery dialog only runs when the launch takes the "recovering" branch. If a lock is held, or an install or a module queue is running, the branch is skipped
and the user lands on Home — where the install marker forces isSystemInstalled() false, so it presents as "no system": no dialog, no Retry, no mention of damage.
LibraryActivity.java:168-177 (the predicate), :187-204 (the redirects that pre-empt it), :287-293 (lock lifts the gate), SystemStateEvaluator:43-45.
Opens with: computing health where it is displayed rather than only in the launch branch. It is already computed app-wide and read by one screen.
6 · DEAD CONTROL — a banked order that is not running is invisible and uncancellable
"See progress" appears only while something is actually running, and a refused or deferred drain leaves the order banked without running. Nothing lists it. The
module sheet's Cancel is the only cancel in the app, and it only inspects the maps and module wishlists — a banked ZIM, Books or Courses order cannot be cancelled.
LibraryHomeFragment.java:518-529 (anyRunning gates the button), :337-342 (isScheduled ignores three of the five wishlists).
7 · DEAD CONTROL — Connect hands out a QR for a box that may not exist
ConnectFragment reads no system fact at all: not isSystemInstalled, not the server state, not the lock. With no system, a damaged one, or the server stopped, the
whole tab behaves normally and prints a QR pointing at a dead port. It is the largest visible-but-useless surface in the app, and the only one with no message.
redesign/ConnectFragment.java — browseUrl():126, no reference to SystemFacts, ServerStateRepository or EnvironmentLock anywhere in the file.
